# Repeated-measures ANOVA: Between-group power calculation
# Design: Two groups, 3 repeated measurements, balanced allocation
# Testing: Subject-level average via pooled t-test (equivalent to between-group F)

library(tidyverse)
library(nlme)  # For flexible covariance structures

# Parameters
mu1 <- 51                    # Group 1 mean
mu2 <- 49                    # Group 2 mean
delta <- mu1 - mu2           # Effect size = 2
sigma_marginal <- 2.5        # Marginal SD at each occasion
k <- 3                       # Number of repeated measurements
rho <- 0.5                   # Compound symmetry correlation
alpha <- 0.05                # Significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.80         # Target power

# Calculate effective variance of the subject-level average under compound symmetry
# Var(Y̅ᵢ) = σ²(1 + (k-1)ρ)/k
effective_var <- sigma_marginal^2 * (1 + (k - 1) * rho) / k
effective_sd <- sqrt(effective_var)

cat("Repeated-Measures ANOVA Analysis\n")
cat("==================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Group 1 mean (μ₁): %.2f\n", mu1))
cat(sprintf("Group 2 mean (μ₂): %.2f\n", mu2))
cat(sprintf("Effect size (Δ = μ₁ - μ₂): %.2f\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("\nMarginal SD at each occasion: %.2f\n", sigma_marginal))
cat(sprintf("Number of repeated measurements: %d\n", k))
cat(sprintf("Compound symmetry correlation (ρ): %.2f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("\nEffective variance of subject-level average:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Var(Y̅ᵢ) = σ²(1 + (k-1)ρ)/k = %.4f² × (1 + %d × %.2f) / %d\n", 
            sigma_marginal, k-1, rho, k))
cat(sprintf("         = %.4f × %.2f / %d\n", sigma_marginal^2, 1 + (k-1)*rho, k))
cat(sprintf("         = %.4f\n", effective_var))
cat(sprintf("Effective SD of subject-level average: %.4f\n\n", effective_sd))

# For a two-sample t-test on subject averages:
# The test statistic is t = (Ȳ₁ - Ȳ₂) / SE where
# SE = effective_sd × sqrt(2/n) for equal group sizes n
# 
# This is equivalent to testing the between-group effect in repeated-measures ANOVA
# using subject-level averages

# Critical value for two-sided test with df ≈ 2n - 2
t_crit_approx <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = 100)  # approximate for larger n
cat(sprintf("Two-sided critical value (two-tailed, α=%.3f): ±%.4f\n\n", alpha, t_crit_approx))

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size per group
calculate_power <- function(n_per_group) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = df)
  se <- effective_sd * sqrt(2 / n_per_group)
  ncp <- delta / se  # Non-centrality parameter
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp)
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size achieving target power
# Start with a reasonable guess
n_candidates <- seq(5, 100, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(n_candidates, calculate_power)

# Find the minimum n where power >= 0.80
minimum_n <- min(n_candidates[powers >= target_power])
power_at_min <- calculate_power(minimum_n)
power_at_prev <- calculate_power(minimum_n - 1)

cat("Sample Size Search Results:\n")
cat("============================\n")
cat(sprintf("Minimum participants per group: %d\n", minimum_n))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power at n=%d: %.6f\n", minimum_n, power_at_min))
cat(sprintf("Power at preceding design (n=%d): %.6f\n\n", minimum_n - 1, power_at_prev))

# Display a range of results for verification
cat("Power Analysis Table:\n")
cat("n\tPower\n")
for (n in seq(minimum_n - 3, minimum_n + 2)) {
  if (n > 0) {
    p <- calculate_power(n)
    cat(sprintf("%d\t%.6f\n", n, p))
  }
}

# Store final results for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_n <- minimum_n
result_power <- power_at_min

cat("\n\nFinal Result:\n")
cat(sprintf("Minimum sample size: %d participants per group\n", result_n))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power: %.6f\n", result_power))

# Parameters
mu1 <- 51
mu2 <- 49
sigma_marginal <- 2.5
k <- 3
rho <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
n_per_group <- 18
n_sim <- 5000

# Compound symmetry covariance matrix
# Σ = σ² [(1-ρ)I + ρ11ᵀ]
Sigma <- sigma_marginal^2 * ((1 - rho) * diag(k) + rho * matrix(1, k, k))

cat("Monte Carlo Simulation Verification\n")
cat("====================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Sample size per group: %d\n", n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("Number of simulations: %d\n", n_sim))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (two-sided): %.3f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Random seed: 42\n\n")

cat("Compound Symmetry Covariance Matrix:\n")
print(round(Sigma, 4))
cat("\n")

# Simulate data and perform tests
rejection_count <- 0

for (sim in 1:n_sim) {
  # Generate data for group 1
  Y1 <- matrix(rnorm(n_per_group * k, mean = mu1), nrow = n_per_group, ncol = k)
  # Apply correlation structure via Cholesky decomposition
  L <- chol(Sigma)
  Y1 <- matrix(rnorm(n_per_group * k), nrow = n_per_group, ncol = k) %*% L + mu1
  
  # Generate data for group 2
  Y2 <- matrix(rnorm(n_per_group * k, mean = mu2), nrow = n_per_group, ncol = k)
  L <- chol(Sigma)
  Y2 <- matrix(rnorm(n_per_group * k), nrow = n_per_group, ncol = k) %*% L + mu2
  
  # Compute subject-level averages
  avg1 <- rowMeans(Y1)
  avg2 <- rowMeans(Y2)
  
  # Perform two-sample t-test on subject averages
  t_result <- t.test(avg1, avg2, var.equal = TRUE)
  p_value <- t_result$p.value
  
  if (p_value < alpha) {
    rejection_count <- rejection_count + 1
  }

ci_upper <- mc_power + 1.96 * mc_se

# Design: Two groups, 3 repeated measurements, balanced allocation
# Testing: Subject-level average via pooled t-test (equivalent to between-group F)

library(nlme)  # For flexible covariance structures

# Parameters

mu2 <- 49                    # Group 2 mean
delta <- mu1 - mu2           # Effect size = 2
sigma_marginal <- 2.5        # Marginal SD at each occasion
k <- 3                       # Number of repeated measurements
rho <- 0.5                   # Compound symmetry correlation
alpha <- 0.05                # Significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.80         # Target power

# Calculate effective variance of the subject-level average under compound symmetry
# Var(Y̅ᵢ) = σ²(1 + (k-1)ρ)/k
effective_var <- sigma_marginal^2 * (1 + (k - 1) * rho) / k
effective_sd <- sqrt(effective_var)

cat("Repeated-Measures ANOVA Analysis\n")
cat("==================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Group 1 mean (μ₁): %.2f\n", mu1))
cat(sprintf("Group 2 mean (μ₂): %.2f\n", mu2))
cat(sprintf("Effect size (Δ = μ₁ - μ₂): %.2f\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("\nMarginal SD at each occasion: %.2f\n", sigma_marginal))
cat(sprintf("Number of repeated measurements: %d\n", k))
cat(sprintf("Compound symmetry correlation (ρ): %.2f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("\nEffective variance of subject-level average:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Var(Y̅ᵢ) = σ²(1 + (k-1)ρ)/k = %.4f² × (1 + %d × %.2f) / %d\n", 
            sigma_marginal, k-1, rho, k))
cat(sprintf("         = %.4f × %.2f / %d\n", sigma_marginal^2, 1 + (k-1)*rho, k))
cat(sprintf("         = %.4f\n", effective_var))
cat(sprintf("Effective SD of subject-level average: %.4f\n\n", effective_sd))

# The test statistic is t = (Ȳ₁ - Ȳ₂) / SE where
# SE = effective_sd × sqrt(2/n) for equal group sizes n
# 
# This is equivalent to testing the between-group effect in repeated-measures ANOVA
# using subject-level averages

# Critical value for two-sided test with df ≈ 2n - 2
t_crit_approx <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = 100)  # approximate for larger n
cat(sprintf("Two-sided critical value (two-tailed, α=%.3f): ±%.4f\n\n", alpha, t_crit_approx))

  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = df)
  se <- effective_sd * sqrt(2 / n_per_group)
  ncp <- delta / se  # Non-centrality parameter
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp)
  return(power)
